# The Helix Center for Interdisciplinary Investigation — Complete Reference

> A 501(c)(3) nonprofit in New York City that hosts free interdisciplinary roundtable discussions bringing together Nobel laureates, MacArthur Fellows, and 519 distinguished scholars across the sciences, humanities, and arts. Founded in 2012 by Dr. Edward Nersessian.

This is the comprehensive companion to llms.txt. It lists every roundtable, speaker, and institution on the site.

## Site Statistics

- 137 roundtable discussions (2012–2026, 15 seasons)
- 519 speakers from 66 institutions
- 112 full transcripts (~1.9 million words)
- 126 YouTube video recordings
- 239 Wikipedia-notable participants
- 4 Nobel laureates, 5 MacArthur Fellows, Pulitzer Prize winners

## All Roundtables

- [Koshin Paley Ellison](https://www.helixcenter.org/speakers/koshin-paley-ellison/) — Co-Founder of the New York Zen Center for Contemplative Care; MFA, LMSW, DMIN, New York Zen Center (Other/Interdisciplin)
- [Morgan Stebbins](https://www.helixcenter.org/speakers/morgan-stebbins/) — Supervising Analyst; Director of Training, Center (Other/Interdisciplin)
- [Amelia Amon](https://www.helixcenter.org/speakers/amelia-amon/) — Principal, Alt.Technica; Solar Designer, Independent (Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Northeast Sustainable Energy Association (NESEA); co-founder of the NY Chapter of the O2 international network for environmentally concerned designers; Chair of the NY Chapter of the Industrial Designers Society of America (IDSA); installations at Liberty Science Center and the Smithsonian)
- [Andrea Bayer](https://www.helixcenter.org/speakers/andrea-bayer/) — Deputy Director for Collections and Administration, The Metropolitan Museum of Art (Former Jayne Wrightsman Curator in the Department of European Paintings; Center for Curatorial Leadership Fellow (Class of 2012); curator of major exhibitions including Painters of Reality (2004), Art and Love in Renaissance Italy (2008-9), and Unfinished: Thoughts Left Visible (2016))
- [Athena Viscusi](https://www.helixcenter.org/speakers/athena-viscusi/) — Psychosocial Care Specialist, MSF/Doctors Without Borders USA (Other/Interdisciplin)
- [Cassie Kaufmann](https://www.helixcenter.org/speakers/cassie-kaufmann/) — Founder and Director, Greene Clinic; Licensed Clinical Psychologist and Psychoanalyst, Greene Clinic / Foundation for Community Psychoanalysis (Founding board member of the Foundation for Community Psychoanalysis; research and publications on psychoanalysis, creativity, art, sexuality, social justice, and politics)
- [Catherine Wikholm](https://www.helixcenter.org/speakers/catherine-wikholm/) — Clinical Psychologist, Private practice in Kent, UK (formerly National Health Service/NHS) (Biology & Medicine)
- [Cheryl Dolinger Brown](https://www.helixcenter.org/speakers/cheryl-dolinger-brown/) — Psychotherapist, LCSW, Independent (Nearly fifty years of clinical practice; dual certification in Somatic Experiencing and the Tapping Method; provides consultations and webinars for mental health professionals)
- [Eva Weil](https://www.helixcenter.org/speakers/eva-weil/) — Psychoanalyst and Researcher, Sorbonne and University Paris I; Centre national de la recherche scientifique (CNRS); University Paris VII; Societe Psychanalytique de Paris (Paris Psychoanalytical Society) (Other/Interdisciplin)
- [Gabrielle Jackson](https://www.helixcenter.org/speakers/gabrielle-jackson/) — Lecturer in Philosophy, Stanford University (Andrew W. Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship at the University of Toronto's Jackman Humanities Institute (2011-2013); Scholar at the Institute for Advanced Study; research on embodiment, motor intentionality, neurophenomenology, and the norms of sex and gender)
- [George Denfield](https://www.helixcenter.org/speakers/george-denfield/) — Psychiatrist and Neuroscientist; Leon Levy Fellow in Neuroscience, Columbia University / New York State Psychiatric Institute (NIMH Outstanding Resident Award; lead author of research published in Nature Communications demonstrating that neuronal variability is attributable to fluctuations in attention; B.S. from Tufts University in biopsychology and cognitive science)
- [Inna Belfer](https://www.helixcenter.org/speakers/inna-belfer/) — Deputy Branch Chief, Basic and Mechanistic Research Branch, National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NCCIH), NIH (Former Associate Professor of Anesthesiology and Human Genetics and Director of the Molecular Epidemiology of Pain Program at the University of Pittsburgh; former clinical reviewer for novel analgesics at the FDA; extensive publications on gene polymorphisms related to pain, psychiatric disorders, and addictions)
- [John Hunter](https://www.helixcenter.org/speakers/john-hunter/) — Educator and Founder, World Peace Game Foundation, Bucknell University, Pennsylvania (Creator of the World Peace Game (1978); TED speaker; presenter at the Aspen Institute, Google, and the United States Pentagon; author of World Peace and Other Fourth-Grade Achievements; subject of a documentary film)
  Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Peace_and_Other_Fourth-Grade_Achievements
- [Ludovica Lumer](https://www.helixcenter.org/speakers/ludovica-lumer/) — Psychoanalyst; Neuroesthetics Researcher, University College London (research affiliate) (Co-author of For Want of Ambiguity: Order and Chaos in Art, Psychoanalysis, and Neuroscience (Bloomsbury, 2021); pioneering research in neuroesthetics with Semir Zeki; co-authored three books on neuroscience, art, and psychoanalysis)
- [Mark Levinson](https://www.helixcenter.org/speakers/mark-levinson/) — Film Director and Producer, Independent (Inaugural Stephen Hawking Medal for Science Communication (2016) for Particle Fever; Particle Fever received 96% approval on Rotten Tomatoes; specialist in ADR post-production, working with directors Anthony Minghella, Francis Coppola, Tom Tykwer, Milos Forman, and Kathryn Bigelow)

Cummings Prize; 2023 Guernsey International Poetry Prize; 2020 NYC Big Book Award (Distinguished Favorite) for 'Field Light')

- [Yonina Hoffman](https://www.helixcenter.org/speakers/yonina-hoffman/) — Assistant Professor of English, United States Merchant Marine Academy (Author of 'The Voices of David Foster Wallace'; research on systems concepts of feedback loops and self-regulation across literature, phenomenology, religion, and environmental studies)
- [Zosia Krusberg](https://www.helixcenter.org/speakers/zosia-krusberg/) — Director of Graduate Studies and Senior Instructional Professor, University of Chicago, Department of Physics (PhD in dark matter phenomenology from University of Chicago; Ed.M. in Mind, Brain, and Education from Harvard; pioneered contemplative practices in undergraduate physics curriculum; practices within the Vajrayana Buddhist tradition)
